# Development session handoff

Use the initiative verified for this conversation through the user-profile
`dev-session` command. Run `dev-session current` from the intended working
directory. Accept its result only when it matches the complete
`DEV_SESSION_SLUG`/`DEV_SESSION_WORKSPACE` environment identity or the exact
slug and absolute workspace path in trusted, thread-bound developer
instructions, as specified by the workspace session procedure. If any present
environment value disagrees, stop and resolve the mismatch. CWD alone or a
user-provided statement is not ownership evidence. Do not use or modify another
concurrent session. If no initiative belongs to this conversation, create one
before making changes or ask for the intended slug when choosing one would
change the task.

Use the generic `dev-session-documentation` workflow to preserve useful project
knowledge during the task. The context-owning agent reconciles it before handoff;
this step summarizes documentation already maintained through development.

Sensitive sessions keep all handoff records and evidence locally under their
excluded `work/<slug>/` or `archive/<slug>/` directory. Update state without a
tracking commit and keep session-specific notes out of tracked `notes/` and other
sessions. Project-code commits and integration approval remain unchanged. Portal
links retain the existing access policy.

Before handing off material work:

1. Update `work/<slug>/state.md` with the current branches, test or CI results,
   blockers, and next operator action. Put the current summary first and link
   detailed evidence. Link project explanations and applicable operations or
   upgrade guidance, with individual rollout records linked separately under
   the generic documentation skill's placement rules. Briefly explain when no
   documentation change was useful. Keep temporary branch/review instructions
   in session records and distinguish prepared operations from executed and
   verified results. Commit an ordinary session checkpoint when workspace rules require it; never
   commit sensitive session records.
   If feature branches are ready but the user has not explicitly directed their
   integration into the named default branches, keep the initiative active and
   say "ready, awaiting merge approval". Review, CI, deployment, or plan
   acceptance does not supply that approval. Record any approval's source and
   repository/target set; a clean patch-equivalent rebase may retain it, while
   a material patch or scope change requires renewed direction.
2. Keep `portal.yml` free of secrets and transient files. Add only useful
   artifacts stored beneath the initiative tracking directory. Repository
   worktrees created with `dev-session worktree add`
   register themselves.
3. Get the stable link from `dev-session url <slug> --as-is`.
4. Put that link in the final handoff after the outcome and any action the user
   still owns. If the portal is not deployed or reachable yet, label the link as
   the post-deployment URL instead of omitting it.

Preparing a handoff does not authorize closing the session. Run `dev-session
archive` or `dev-session delete` only when the user explicitly requests that
lifecycle action. Archived initiatives retain the same URL and become read-only
until `dev-session revive` restores them.

Establish whether each migration version was merged, released, deployed, or
externally consumed before rewriting it. Consolidate obsolete, unapplied branch
history while preserving supported paths. Give this inventory to the dedicated
independent reviewer for an explicit whole-branch history and migration
conclusion under the mandatory-change-review workflow. Earlier incremental
reviews do not complete this gate.

Consolidate repeated dependency or channel-pin updates in one logical update
stream into one final update, including generated lockfiles and metadata.
Identify streams by the dependency, channel/role or input and their logical
purpose. Branch publication, development deployment and earlier incremental
review do not justify retaining superseded pins. Preserve supported deployed
behavior and migration lineage; that compatibility obligation does not require
keeping each intermediate pin commit. Retain separate updates only when a
concrete release, supported consumer or state boundary requires them, with
evidence explaining why the final update alone is insufficient. Keep rollout
SHAs and execution evidence in rollout records. If a supported consumer needs
an exact source revision, preserve its required ref as part of consolidation.
Existing published-history protections still apply.

Include these streams and their commit dispositions in the review packet under
the mandatory-change-review skill. The reviewer must independently assess
consolidation and any retained boundary; a mechanical-content review exemption
does not exempt commits from whole-branch history assessment.

Immediately before an approved merge, the lead checks the current complete
base-to-head series and final diff against the final review. Confirm that
superseded updates were consolidated and any retained updates have the required
evidence and reviewer conclusion. Record the checked final heads and history
conclusion in session state. For later changes, apply the skill's existing
narrow-fix and affected-lane review rules and this procedure's patch-equivalent
rebase rules; do not substitute an earlier incremental review for the final
series check. Integration still requires explicit user approval.

Before changing code in a repository, read its local `AGENTS.md` if present.
When a repository has no `AGENTS.md`, infer commands and style from its
existing files, history, and manifests.


## Retained branches with unknown historical bases

An ordinary registration may omit `initial_base_sha` honestly. Re-add its exact
existing branch without supplying a guessed base; missing retained refs require
explicit recovery and cannot become new branches at today's default. Registration
and sync do not infer historical starts from merge-base or current tips. `--base`
selects a genuinely new branch's start. For a retained historical base, use the
workspace's [dated source-only repair](../maintenance/repair-legacy-sessions-2026-10-04.md)
with exact structured commit/blob and repository/branch evidence. Finalization
still requires the exact final head; unknown bases do not earn the unpushed-initial-head archive exception. A saved
exact comparison remains useful, otherwise archived comparison is unavailable.

# Knowledge-base and user-facing writing

Required workspace procedure, selected by the routing table in `AGENTS.md`.

DokuWiki user documentation is hosted at `kb.vpsfree.cz` and
`kb.vpsfree.org`. Their review instances are
`kb-cs.aitherdev.int.vpsfree.cz` and `kb-en.aitherdev.int.vpsfree.cz`. API
access to production uses one token per wiki:

When authoring or translating Czech KB pages, address the reader using
informal singular forms (`tykání`), for example `můžeš`, `potřebuješ`,
`nainstaluj`, and `použij`. Do not use formal `vy` or plural imperatives as a
polite form; use plural only when genuinely addressing multiple people.

The invisible DokuWiki `<page>` tag connects Czech and English translations.
Use the same tag value in every language variant, and always derive it from the
English KB page ID. The real DokuWiki page IDs remain language-specific.

For all user-facing prose, use the workspace skill in
`~/.codex/skills/vpsfree-user-facing-writing/SKILL.md`. This applies to KB pages,
vpsAdmin documentation and interface copy, user-visible errors and help, mail
templates, website copy, and member-facing release or operational messages.
The agent that owns the task context must apply the skill directly after the
technical content is settled and before committing. Do not delegate the main
rewrite to a context-poor subagent; a fresh agent may review the finished text.
Human-readable comments in bilingual scripts and configuration examples must
use the language of the surrounding page while commands and machine-significant
content remain equivalent.

Write KB pages as documentation of the current supported state. Do not
mention obsolete distributions, former defaults, superseded commands, or
historical workarounds unless readers of a still-supported installation need
that history to migrate or recover. Record removal rationale in commit
messages, DokuWiki revision summaries, or initiative notes instead of page
prose.

For vpsAdmin changes that can affect visible WebUI documentation, follow the
canonical workflow in `vpsfree-kb-contracts/docs/webui-change-workflow.md`.
Use `kb-contract-fetch`, `kb-contract-build`, and
`kb-contract-manifest` for durable all-page candidate preparation; keep

repository.

Do not merge a `vpsfree-kb-contracts` feature branch merely to make managed-page
links work in staging. Managed release manifests pin the committed and pushed
feature revision, and staging resolves `<kb-managed>` links at that exact
commit. Before production promotion, integrate the contract changes into

- `kb.vpsfree.cz`:
  `/home/aither/.codex/codex-kb-vpsfree-cz-aither-key`
- `kb.vpsfree.org`:

Never copy credentials into notes, commits, command output, URLs, or prompts.

The declarative `kb-staging` NixOS container on aitherdev is global and

by the active `DEV_SESSION_SLUG`; do not manipulate another session's

releases ownership while retaining the data. It refuses a pending review
bundle unless `--discard-pending` is explicit.

Stage complete pages at their real page IDs so links and language mappings are

and `--approved-production`. Individual production writes with `kb-page`
also require `--approved-production`, including writes in `drafts:`. Read-only
production checks do not require approval. Before every write, verify
authentication and page permission against the exact target wiki.

such as "Publish reviewed KB release" for new edits. Write summaries for

vysvětlit správu obsahu v repozitáři`. Do not rewrite existing DokuWiki
revision summaries merely to adopt this convention.

Page deletions belong in the same guarded schema-5 release manifest as page
writes. Stage and review their localized summaries and revision histories, then
promote the exact manifest after approval. Do not delete release pages with
separate `kb-page` calls. New `kb-cleanup` manifests must use schema 2 and give
every page deletion its own summary; media deletions do not have summaries.

Common KB tool examples:

kb-stage start

kb-release stage --manifest work/example/kb-release.yml --yes

# Project map

## Project Map

These repositories are in scope for this workspace:

- `dev-workspace`: reusable development-session lifecycle, user-profile
  runtime, host module and portal shell. Its
  canonical remote is `git@github.com:aither64/dev-workspace.git`.
- `vpsfree-dev-workspace`: vpsFree.cz KB commands, workspace skills,
  development-cluster providers and migration tooling. Its canonical remote is
  `git@github.com:vpsfreecz/dev-workspace.git`; concrete site configuration is
  supplied by this workspace.
- `codex-web`: reusable Go client, capability-checked HTTP integration and
  framework-free browser module for Codex App Server. Its canonical remote is
  `git@github.com:aither64/codex-web.git`.
- `vpsadminos`: NixOS, ZFS, and LXC-based host OS for containers. It is the
  core runtime for vpsFree.cz nodes and many integration tests.
- `vpsadmin`: Ruby/PHP control panel and API for managing VPSes on top of
  vpsAdminOS.
- `security-advisories`: evidence-backed vpsFree.cz platform security
  assessments, including vpsAdmin Node evidence collection, advisory
  evaluation, and preparation of unpublished vpsAdmin drafts.
- `vpsfree-kb-contracts`: independent, reproducible Czech/English page,
  runtime-test, screenshot, and WebUI documentation contracts for an explicit
  subset of the vpsFree.cz knowledge bases. Its canonical
  `docs/webui-change-workflow.md` must be followed when a vpsAdmin feature can
  change visible labels, navigation, forms, layout, or screenshots.
- `ruby-lxc`: Ruby native extension wrapping liblxc. It is consumed by
  vpsAdminOS `osctld` and may need coordinated gem releases for Ruby or LXC
  upgrades.
- `haveapi`: framework for self-describing APIs. It underpins vpsAdmin's API
  shape and client generation.
- `vpsf-status`: Go status page and monitoring-facing status service for
  vpsFree.cz.
- `vpsadmin-go-client`: generated Go client library for the vpsAdmin API.
- `confctl`: Ruby/Nix deployment management tool used with NixOS and
  vpsAdminOS fleets.
- `vpsfree-cz-configuration`: production vpsFree.cz cluster configuration in
  Nix.
- `vpsadminos-org-configuration`: vpsadminos.org cluster configuration in Nix.
- `vpsfree-irc-bot`: IRC bot for vpsFree.cz channels and infrastructure
  integration.
- `vpsfree-mail-templates`: localized mail templates consumed by vpsAdmin.
- `terraform-provider-vpsadmin`: Go Terraform/OpenTofu provider for vpsAdmin.
- `web`: PHP and server-side-include website for vpsFree.cz and its
  translations.
- `ssh-exporter`: Prometheus exporter that checks systems over SSH and exports
  metrics.
- `syslog-exporter`: Prometheus exporter that parses syslog streams into
  metrics.
- `vpsfree-client`: Ruby CLI and client library for the vpsFree.cz API, built
  on vpsAdmin and HaveAPI clients.
- `vpsfree-maintenance-tasks`: dated operational scripts for maintenance work.
- `linux`: Linux kernel tree used by vpsAdminOS. Treat it as reference material
  unless the task explicitly targets kernel work.
- `zfs`: OpenZFS tree used by vpsAdminOS. Treat it as reference material unless
  the task explicitly targets ZFS work.

Common dependency flow: HaveAPI defines the API framework and client-generation
model. vpsAdmin consumes HaveAPI and manages infrastructure running on
vpsAdminOS. The Go client, Ruby client, and Terraform provider consume the
vpsAdmin API. The configuration repositories deploy NixOS and vpsAdminOS
systems, usually with confctl. Status, exporters, web, IRC bot, mail templates,
and maintenance tasks support operations around the core platform. This
coordination workspace selects `dev-workspace`, which in turn consumes
`codex-web`; keep that dependency direction one-way.
# Session setup and tracking

Required workspace procedure, selected by the routing table in `AGENTS.md`.
Its rules retain workspace scope and precedence. Paths and commands are relative
to the coordination workspace unless the text specifies another repository.

## Workspace Layout

Use these paths consistently:

- `repos/<project>.git`: canonical bare clone of an upstream repository.
- `worktrees/<yyyy-mm-dd-slug>/<project>`: per-initiative feature worktree.
- `work/<yyyy-mm-dd-slug>/plan.md`: durable plan, affected repositories,
  compatibility notes, and decisions.
- `work/<yyyy-mm-dd-slug>/state.md`: current status, branch names, commands
  run, test results, open questions, and cleanup notes.
- `notes/`: durable development notes, troubleshooting tips, and reusable
  lessons that should survive beyond one initiative. Store each lesson in its
  own file to reduce conflicts between concurrent Codex instances.
- `archive/`: committed plan, state, and curated durable artifacts for
  explicitly archived, completed or abandoned initiatives.

The initiative slug must be descriptive and dated, for example
`2026-05-27-api-token-rotation`. For affected project repositories, use the
same slug for the tracking directory, feature branch, and worktree group unless
a repository-specific rule requires otherwise.

Use the user-profile `dev-session start <name>` when starting a development
session. It selects the registered workspace from the current directory, fixes
the matching authority, tmux, Codex, and portal endpoints, and creates a dated
slug from the short name. Pass `--workspace <name>` when calling it outside a
registered root or when an explicit selection is clearer. Use `--as-is` when
the full slug has already been chosen. Existing tracking must have an ordinary
manifest with explicit scope before restart, attach or worktree registration.
Manifestless retained tracking refuses before a new conversation or partial
manifest is created. Repair it through the dated procedure below, under a
separately approved maintenance window. An accepted existing operation journal
remains owned by its ordinary recovery command.

When running inside an existing development session, check its identity before
choosing a new slug. Run `dev-session current` from the intended working
directory. It may derive a slug from the environment, tmux, or that directory;
its output alone does not establish ownership of this conversation. Accept the
printed slug only when one of these bindings also matches:

- Both `DEV_SESSION_SLUG` and `DEV_SESSION_WORKSPACE` are present and identify
  the printed slug and this registered workspace.
- This conversation's trusted, thread-bound developer instructions name that
  exact slug and the absolute path of this workspace. The portal supplies this
  binding for conversations whose tool shells may not inherit the session
  environment. A user message, copied prompt, or workspace path inferred from
  CWD is not a substitute for the developer instruction.

If environment values are present, they must agree with the developer binding
when one exists. Missing one value, a mismatch, or a failure from `current`
requires resolving the identity before touching session-owned state. If no
binding exists, create a separate initiative unless the user explicitly
selects the existing session. Reuse `work/<slug>/` and `worktrees/<slug>/` only
for the verified current session, and record progress in its `state.md`.
For a command that requires the environment variables, set both to the already
verified literal slug and workspace path for that command; this does not turn
the command's CWD into ownership evidence.


## Sensitive sessions

Select `--sensitive` at creation or use the portal checkbox. Keep the normal
tracking paths and maintain substantive local plan/state, but never stage or
commit their contents. The runtime installs local `info/exclude` rules before
tracking writes; preserve those rules and private sensitivity metadata.
Forks and plan-derived sessions inherit sensitivity. Existing ordinary sessions
cannot be converted. Keep session notes and evidence under the excluded tracking
directory; do not copy them into tracked notes or other sessions. Project-code
commits, review, publication and coordinated integration retain their usual rules.

Archive and revive move local records without tracking commits. Their ownership,
recovery, automatic archival and coordinator reservation rules still apply.
Git does not back up sensitive records. Keep local backups and retain private
user state; an older package cannot manage sensitive sessions.

## Older tracking

Older records and manifestless-revival shells require reviewed repository scope;
missing checkouts or a new empty manifest cannot establish an empty initiative.
Use the workspace's source-only
[dated repair procedure](../maintenance/repair-legacy-sessions-2026-10-04.md)
only within an explicitly assigned scope. Keep original prose, artifacts, exact
retained root/team and all structured/exact-slug obligations. Do not invent
creation/goals metadata or a historical branch base to make a record eligible.
After repair, ordinary readiness depends on explicit scope and exact current
identity/native/receipt proof, without a repair marker or private provenance
reader. Present creation evidence keeps its genuine completion contract.
Lost browser revive success/journal evidence cannot be certified by repair.

## Planning And Tracking

Start each requested feature or fix by identifying the affected projects. Some
features span multiple repositories; plan the cross-repository shape before
editing any one component.

For each initiative, maintain:

- `plan.md`: the goal, affected components, approach, compatibility analysis,
  deployment ordering, testing plan, and explicit decisions.
- `state.md`: branch/worktree locations, current progress, commands run,
  results, blockers, and cleanup status.

Treat `work/<slug>/` as active tracking and `archive/<slug>/` as terminal
tracking. New `state.md` files must begin with this exact YAML front matter:

```yaml
---
lifecycle: active
---
```

An initiative remains `active` while any registered feature branch is
unmerged or the session still owns work. Set it to `complete` only after every
registered branch's exact final head is merged into its configured remote
default branch and no review, CI, deployment, approval, or cleanup remains.
Pushing, testing, deploying, or temporarily removing worktrees does not make an
initiative complete. Use `abandoned` only when the work is explicitly
discarded; abandoned work does not have to be merged. Coordination-only
initiatives with no registered branches can still be completed. Explicit user archival uses `archived` to close unfinished or integrated work
without claiming completion or discard. The anchored
front matter is the only lifecycle authority; lifecycle-looking text in the
Markdown body has no effect.

Completion criteria do not authorize integration. When feature work is ready
but the user has not explicitly approved its repository/target set for merging,
keep `lifecycle: active` and put "ready, awaiting merge approval" near the top
of `state.md`. Record any approval's wording/source, repository and target
branches, whether a later rebase preserved patch equivalence, and the exact
final heads once integrated. Do not mark an initiative complete merely because
review, CI, or deployment succeeded.

For ordinary sessions, write a substantive plan and initial state, then commit both in the top-level
workspace repository before the first project-code commit or external mutation.
After that initial commit, keep plan and state current in the working tree
without committing every update. A short initiative should normally make no
further tracking-only commit until its final archive commit. If an initiative
remains unfinished at the end of an active working day, it may make at most one
consolidated tracking-only checkpoint for that day when material progress is
worth preserving. This is a ceiling, not a daily requirement. Material progress
includes changed implementation heads, durable decisions, completed phases,
new blockers, and results that change the next step.

An additional same-day tracking checkpoint is allowed only for a genuine
ownership handoff or an explicit user request. A pause until a future working

Individual plan edits, branch-head changes, review findings or remediations,
commands, test or CI results, deployment actions, and status polls do not by
themselves require commits; consolidate them into the next daily, handoff, or
final summary. Functional changes in the workspace repository and normal
commits in project repositories do not count as tracking-only checkpoints.

Keep these files current enough that a future agent can resume the work without
guessing. When plans change because code or tests reveal new facts, update the
tracking notes.

`work/<slug>/design.md` before substantive implementation. The

Routine planning, investigation, findings, session tracking and evidence alone
never trigger automatic review. Explicitly requested earlier review is advisory

substantive documentation and configuration deliverables remain in scope.

current. Register or update artifacts with
`dev-session artifact add <slug> <path> --label "Caption" --as-is` instead of
hand-editing artifact YAML. This uses the validated atomic writer and preserves
the session's identity and repository scope. Include the stable link printed by
`dev-session url <slug> --as-is` in the handoff. If the portal has not been

Promote reusable lessons to `notes/`. In particular, write a note when a
command, shell, test, build, deploy, hook, or worktree operation fails in a

# Development environment and verification

Required workspace procedure, selected by the routing table in `AGENTS.md`.
Its rules retain workspace scope and precedence. Paths and commands are relative
to the coordination workspace unless the text specifies another repository.

For queued merges/deployments, complete builds, tests and review before submitting
the prepared snapshot. Resource contention is a wait, not a failed check. Follow
[coordination](../coordination.md) for interruptible waiting and stale-snapshot
refresh; repeat only the checks/review required by the changed patch or baseline.

Use separately exported Ruby checks and retained derivation/input receipts to
reuse exact successful verification. Tree equality alone does not justify reuse.
The aggregate Ruby check must prove complete unique shard coverage; preserve the
unsharded diagnostic mode. Run independent checks concurrently where safe.
An integration driver that also approves/submits/activates operations is launched
by the lead. A verification utility may observe its independent logs/status; it
must not launch or resume that mutation driver itself.

## Development Environment

Use the generic `dev-session-monitor` skill for authorized tests, CI checks and
builds expected to exceed one minute, and delegate uncertain-duration integration
tests and builds before launching them. Resolve the fresh verification watcher
from the installed catalog's separate utility policy. It is not a team member
and must not edit source, diagnose, retry, approve, or deploy.
Keep known quick checks inline. Resolve planning, implementation and diagnosis
settings from the retained team roster. Mandatory review uses an eligible
retained review-purpose member's saved model and effort; without one, use a
review-purpose role from the installed catalog's default development team in a
fresh standalone thread, including for solo sessions. Do not invent a team or
change the roster. Run final review only after the substantive deliverable is
complete, all intended changes are committed, and quick checks pass, before
long integration tests. Completed substantive documentation and configuration
deliverables remain in scope. Routine planning, investigation, findings,
session tracking and evidence alone never trigger automatic review. Earlier
review requires an explicit user request, is advisory, and does not replace
final review. A reviewer in a preset receives no automatic assignment. Pass
project escalation rules, including
unexpected local kernel builds, in the watcher's brief. The parent continues
automatically on completion or escalation. If the skill or delegation is
unavailable, report
that once and use minimal-output parent monitoring. A user's instruction not to
wait for CI takes precedence.

Development is generally Nix-based. Prefer each repository's `nix develop`,
`nix-shell`, flake outputs, or documented development shell before running
language-specific tools. Deployment is usually to NixOS or vpsAdminOS systems,
often through `confctl` and the configuration repositories.

Treat an unexpected local Linux kernel build in vpsAdminOS development or test
workflows as a bug unless the current work intentionally changes kernel sources
or configuration. vpsAdminOS kernels should normally be substituted from the
vpsAdminOS binary cache after GitHub Actions or its runners build them. When a
command starts building a kernel, stop it and investigate why the derivation
missed the cache. A local rebuild is acceptable only when the kernel or its
configuration is intentionally changed, or when the responsible runner has not
yet built and published the expected derivation; record the justification in
the initiative `state.md`.
If the work needs an additional kernel output, update the vpsAdminOS CI builder
to build and publish that output as part of the same initiative instead of
relying on recurring local builds.

When running `vpsadmin-devcluster`, use the bridge network by
default. Do not choose `--network local` unless the user explicitly asks for it
or the bridge network is genuinely unavailable; if local networking is used,
record the reason in the initiative state.

Use GitHub Actions as a feedback loop after pushing branches. If `gh` is not
available in the current shell, run it through Nix, for example
`nix shell nixpkgs#gh -c gh run list ...`. Inspect failed logs, monitor reruns,
and resolve failures instead of leaving CI for the user to chase.
Successful checks, review, and CI are verification evidence, not permission to
merge or push feature content to a default branch; follow the Git approval gate.
Before calling an unmerged feature branch ready, give the independent reviewer
its complete cleaned base-to-head commit series, final diff, and migration
provenance under the mandatory-change-review workflow. Require explicit
conclusions on obsolete history and migration lineage, including "no migrations"
when applicable.
Record findings and remaining deployment limits in the initiative state.

After a force-push or a follow-up fix push, cancel superseded queued or
in-progress GitHub Actions workflow runs for the same branch. Only cancel runs
whose `headSha` no longer matches the current branch head; do not cancel
workflows for other branches or workflows already running on the current head.

When creating or editing GitHub workflows, verify the latest upstream version of
each imported action from its official repository before choosing the `uses:`
ref. Do not rely on remembered version numbers; use the newest compatible
version unless the workflow records a specific reason to pin an older one.

Rerunning a failed GitHub Actions job is not a substitute for investigation.
Before accepting a rerun as validation, download or open the failed attempt's
logs and artifacts, identify the root cause as far as the available evidence
allows, and record the finding in the initiative `state.md`. If the artifacts
are insufficient, improve the test or runner diagnostics rather than treating a
green rerun as proof that the failure did not matter. Prefer fixing the
underlying problem; when the failure is unrelated to the current change, record
the evidence for that conclusion.

When a repository is missing a tool in the ambient shell, enter the repository's
Nix shell or use an appropriate `nix shell` command. Do not work around missing
tooling by recording local environment limitations in commit messages.

When adding new integration tests that use the vpsAdminOS test-runner, write
test scripts in the current RSpec-style structure with examples and
expectations, such as `describe`, `it`, and `expect`. Do not refactor existing
tests solely to convert their style unless the user explicitly asks for that
refactor.

# Configuration and development deployment

Required workspace procedure, selected by the routing table in `AGENTS.md`.

to the coordination workspace unless the text specifies another repository.

The selected package also provides the authoritative installed guides through
`workspace-host coordination guide`, including before workspace integration.

Before deployment activation or a workspace profile switch, read
[coordination](../coordination.md) in full. Build and copy outside execution
claims; activate through the exact owner's approved jobs and machine reservation.

In every confctl-managed configuration repository, inspect its defined
channels and the channel-to-input mapping before updating a flake input. For a
normal update to a published upstream revision, run
`confctl inputs channel update --commit <channel> [role]` for the affected
channel and role. Use `confctl inputs channel set --commit <channel> <role> <rev>`
when an exact unmerged feature revision must be pinned. Do not manually edit
`flake.lock` or update the input outside its channel when a channel owns it.
Verify the generated lock diff has the intended revisions and no unrelated
input changes, accounting for expected transitive lock changes.

Keep confctl's generated Git history in the update commit message. Leave its
changelog enabled when useful; use `--no-changelog` for noisy inputs such as
`nixpkgs` and `llm-agents`. Keep automated `confctl ... --commit` messages as
generated, even when a line exceeds generic commit-message width rules. Edit
one only when intentionally making a concise changelog correction.

Deployment does not authorize integration into any repository's default branch;
the Git procedure requires explicit user direction for the repository/target
set before feature-content integration. Build and deploy development
configurations directly from the initiative worktree and feature branch. In
particular, while the workspace
portal is still under development, keep its `vpsfree-cz-configuration` changes
on the dated initiative branch. The workspace application itself is deployed
from its own user profile and must not be added to, pinned by, or iterated
through the system configuration. Do not merge or push configuration changes
to `master` merely to deploy aitherdev. Integrate that branch only after the
user explicitly directs the merge; accepting a plan or deployment result alone
is insufficient.

## Workspace runtime selection

The workspace owns generic runtime selection through
`inputs.vpsfree-dev-workspace.inputs.dev-workspace.url` in `flake.nix`.
This direct nested URL keeps the selected extension source independent of the
runtime revision. Extension updates must preserve that selection unless a
reviewed composition change intentionally replaces it. Remove the override only
when the selected extension provides the intended runtime and review proves that
the effective input graph and package/deployment contracts remain equivalent.

Select a published exact runtime revision, then generate the composed lock in
the workspace feature worktree with
`nix flake update vpsfree-dev-workspace/dev-workspace`. Inspect semantic input
paths and locked identities: preserve the extension revision/content hash,
sibling inputs and existing follows paths. Do not add a top-level runtime input,
rewrite the extension's own lock or deduplicate dependency nodes incidentally.
The direct nested runtime must match configuration's `devWorkspace` selection,
managed through its existing confctl channel. Run
`bin/check-dev-workspace-deployment --workspace-root PATH --configuration-root PATH`
against the final locks before deployment. The application still comes from the
workspace user profile; configuration selects the matching host module/runtime
contract and does not install the application.
# Commits and hooks

Required workspace procedure, selected by the routing table in `AGENTS.md`.
Its rules retain workspace scope and precedence. Paths and commands are relative
to the coordination workspace unless the text specifies another repository.

## Commits

Write informative commits. A commit message must explain what is changing and
why it is needed. The subject should summarize the change; the body should
explain the problem, rationale, and deployment or compatibility notes when that
context matters. Do not add command transcripts, "Checks:", "Tests:",
"Syntax checks:", "Validated with:", or local tool availability notes to commit
messages; record validation in `state.md` or PR notes instead.

Rules:

- Wrap every commit message line at 80 characters or fewer. Generated
  `confctl ... --commit` messages in `vpsfree-cz-configuration` are the
  exception: keep them exactly as generated, even when they exceed this limit.
- Always write the commit message to a temporary file and commit with
  `git commit -F <tmpfile>`.
- Do not use `git commit -m` for final commits.
- Pre-commit hooks are mandatory, not advisory. Before the first commit in a
  repository or worktree, verify that the repository's hook framework is
  installed and active when the repository declares one, for example
  `.overcommit.yml`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `lefthook.yml`, or Husky
  configuration. Install hooks with the repository-documented command, or infer
  the standard framework command when documentation is missing.
- Do not commit when expected hooks are absent, fail, or cannot be run. Fix the
  hook setup or the reported offenses first. Only continue without hooks when
  the user explicitly authorizes it for that commit, and record the reason and
  replacement checks in the initiative state.
- Running syntax checks or selected tests is not a substitute for hook-managed
  lint/format checks. If a hook framework cannot be installed but the
  equivalent command is known, run that command manually before committing and
  record that fallback in state.
- Do not bypass git hooks unless the user explicitly authorizes it and the
  reason is recorded in the initiative state.
- Keep commits focused. Split generated updates, dependency bumps, release
  metadata, and functional changes when repository rules or review clarity call
  for it.
- Respect each repository's local commit subject style and special release or
  generated-file rules.
# 2026-10-12-streamline-vpsadminos-config-imports

## Goal

NixOS VPS (containers) on vpsAdminOS need to import vpsadminos.nix from vpsAdminOS into their configuration, since it contains settings needed for our environment. Different NixOS releases have different options, sometimes incompatible, so the users must import the right version of that config for their system. I'd like you to check if it is streamlined as much as possible, e.g. I guess we could import configs based on the user's nixpkgs release version. Do we do it currently?

## Affected repositories

- `vpsadminos`: flake module exports, stable guest templates, focused evaluation
  tests/CI, and owning-project documentation.
- Czech and English KB pages: NixOS, Impermanence, and User Data. These six pages
  are unmanaged; no managed-page expansion is needed.
- `vpsfree-kb-contracts`: final review identified a baseline missing dataset-create
  annotation/binding in both Impermanence pages. Add existing-path page bindings,
  expected tag counts, and scoped discovery reconciliation for the candidates.
  No WebUI controls, screenshots, managed pages or production input changes.

## Approach

Implement the accepted refinement (user: "Implement the plan", 2026-10-15).
The independent Astra/xhigh whole-approach review supports retaining the guest
adapter but identified missing ancestor/direct-filesystem coverage. Architect0
records the revised design before implementer0 edits application code. The lead
restores the six instruction files, reconciles the guest guide and logical patch
versions/history, and coordinates final review and exact-head verification.

Retain the original accepted selector plan (2026-10-14). Architect0
records the design and verification brief before implementer0 edits application
files. The lead prepares bilingual KB candidates and coordinates verification,
review, publication of the feature branch, and the guarded KB review workflow.

One release registry drives the grouped exact-release exports, old underscore
aliases, and the release-aware stable selector. Stable templates import
`nixosModules.containerStable`; selection occurs when the guest evaluates its
nixpkgs, rather than when the image is built.

## Decisions

- Use the upstream default branch, `staging`, rather than the older `master`.
- Expose `nixosModules.containers."26.05"` and dynamic lookup by release string.
- Both modern `container` and `containerStable` select a registered stable
  release using the guest module-system `lib.trivial.release`. No containerAuto.
- Retain all eight underscore exports (22.11 through 26.05).
- Unknown releases fail during evaluation with actionable instructions. Unstable
  remains explicit through `containerUnstable`; do not guess from version suffix.
- Preserve legacy `nixosConfigurations` semantics and standalone compatibility
  files, including the root assertion file.
- Update six KB pages. Search found the conversion only in bilingual
  Impermanence; bilingual User Data has a related legacy module import.
- Initial metadata refusal is resolved: the ordinary manifest is now schema 1,
  creation ready; architect assignments succeeded during planning.
- Required narrow final-review correction: annotate existing subdataset-create
  instructions in steps 3 and 5 with `datasets.create.open`, count two tags per
  language, and bind both pages; refresh affected
  inventory only. The main technical interface and guest behavior are unchanged.
- Runtime testing exposed an independent impermanence UID-after-restart failure
  on unchanged raw/unstable compatibility paths. Diagnostics are authorized;
  the user now authorizes fixing it in this initiative: "all right, fix it as
  part of our work. find the root cause however, let's not create workaround
  without understanding the issue". Establish the runtime map/mount/activation
  cause before selecting the correction. The prior proposal is a candidate,
  not a prescribed implementation. Architect0 updates the accepted design once
  the cause is established; implementer0 implements a separate logical baseline
  fix with focused regression, final review and runtime verification. Preserve
  dynamic allocation, original numeric ownership and all fixture assertions.
- Cause established by v2 runtime evidence: allocation precedes late exposure
  of intact persistent maps. The accepted revision uses the upstream globally ordered specialfs callback
  to prepare/check effective early mounts covering /var/lib/nixos or /var/log,
  with a native dependency before legacy users. Root is not an activation
  trigger. See design.md for binding, predecessor and filesystem semantics.

## Accepted whole-approach refinement

- Select from effective enabled boot.specialFileSystems after module merging;
  include /var, /var/lib and direct filesystem declarations with component-aware
  matching. Keep upstream global order and source its script once.
- Compute required predecessor membership using the existing utils.fsBefore
  relation. Fail closed for those callbacks without a second sorter, phase,
  replay or runtime failure journal. Unrelated callbacks retain their behavior.
- Check directory-bind identity and mount results; selected binds may prepare
  missing sources. Required predecessor binds do not create missing sources.
  Non-bind filesystems use native mount/remount plus status/mountpoint checks,
  without treating device names as directories or claiming device durability.
- The user explicitly chose root/0755 bootstrap defaults. Custom owner AND mode
  require pre-provisioning; impermanence does not later apply requested metadata
  to pre-created sources. Preserve existing metadata and the recursive helper,
  whose per-parent modes differ from mkdir-p under inherited default ACLs.
- Restore all initiative instruction amendments in product20b803f,
  workspaceabacb121 and extension9d2ae656. Retain exact backups, preserve unrelated
  work, remove instruction-only shipping owners and restore truthful logical
  patch versions/history. Keep selector and baseline persistence independent.
- Preserve the current eight runtime cases; add /var, /var/lib and direct-bind
  adoption plus fresh ancestor initialization. Ancestor fixtures omit exact
  state/log binds. Use layout-owned mount/backing expectations, explicit0755,
  pre-existing0710 and payload-directory0750 assertions. Add real nonbind and
  required-remount refusal controls with unchanged IDs/maps/data.
- Commit with declared hooks and pass normal quick checks, then obtain the same
  independent Astra review of final source/history before long runtime checks.
  Fresh Luna/low utilities own long verification. Prior20b evidence remains
  revision-scoped; revised acceptance is pending. No merge/deploy/KB publication.

## Compatibility and deployment

The intentional semantic change is confined to modern generic stable imports:
they previously used the latest stable file and will select the guest's release.
Old/future/custom unregistered releases will fail rather than receive a fallback.
Explicit versioned imports and legacy configuration exports retain their targets.

No persisted-state, database/schema/seed, API/client/CLI/Terraform, daemon
protocol, host or node change is needed. No coordinated all-machine update is
required. The selector retains each release module's configuration behavior;
the independent correction changes activation timing in the four supported raw
files. system.stateVersion and map formats stay intact. Selected sources on
persistent root or separate storage remain supported; global mount ordering is
preserved. Declared early covering mounts are checked, while undeclared host
storage remains the host responsibility. Existing metadata is preserved. This prevents new identity drift without repairing affected guests;
an old-generation restart can reintroduce the ordering defect.

Adoption is per guest through its input update/rebuild. Existing configuration
files are written only when absent and are not rewritten. Public KB examples
must wait for availability of the new exports in the public default source.
Rollback below the new interface reverts imports and vpsadminos pin together;
existing NixOS generations remain available. This work does not authorize
integration into staging or production KB publication; these have explicit
approval gates. No production guest or host deployment is planned.

## Documentation

Owning-project guest documentation explains automatic, exact-release and
unstable imports, supported registry keys, errors, legacy exports, and the
standalone-file path. Link it from the docs index. KB prose is maintained by the
lead with the user-facing writing skill; preserve page IDs, language mappings,
code semantics and unrelated content. Prepare six complete candidates and
localized summaries in one bilingual review bundle. Session records own branch
and rollout evidence, review packet, verification results and approval status.

## Testing plan

Quick checks: all release keys/aliases, pure selector matrix and actionable
unknown-release errors, real guest evaluations for 24.11/25.11/26.05, old
stateVersion and differing host-input/guest releases, release upgrade without
editing import, explicit unstable, four generated flakes/locks, standalone-file
evaluation, KB example syntax, documentation and declared hooks. Focused leaf
tests are required because flake checking does not descend into the grouped map.

Commit all intended source/documentation and candidate changes, inventory final
base-to-head history/diff and migration provenance (none), then assign reviewer0
the mandatory final review before long integration tests. Preserve narrow-fix
review policy. A fresh Luna/low watcher launches/monitors the four current
stable/unstable ordinary/impermanence image cases; verify rebuild, network/DNS,
restart, persistent data and stable UID/GID/machine-id for impermanence. Stop an
unexpected local kernel build under the verification procedure. No full host
suite is needed unless evidence justifies it.

## Superseded compatibility and instruction revision

The user previously approved this follow-up plan with "Implement the plan".
Its instruction amendments and exact-target selection are superseded by the
2026-10-15 refinement above; its removal of invented backing restrictions and
separate mount phases remains applicable. Revise the
persistence fix to retain existing storage layouts and NixOS's complete mount
order. Non-root backing and split-topology restrictions are superseded. The
whole-value specialfs priority90 seam passed build-free evaluation on real
25.11/26.05/unstable, including dry behavior and guest mkForce precedence.
Architect0 records the implementation brief before implementer0 edits source.

Added affected repositories: workspace instructions (dedicated workspace
worktree) and vpsfree-dev-workspace's maintained review-skill source. Amend
commit policy to require finished behavior/rationale/compatibility without
revision labels, development diaries or temporary validation status. Preserve
true upstream provenance. Tighten review for normal test execution and
unnecessary compatibility restrictions. Rewrite the two current source owners'
messages; retain semantic separation and exact tested-head backups.

Expose focused persistence checks as normal flake checks with explicit inputs,
remove session-specific baseline environment hooks from shipping tests, and
register an RSpec old-to-new upgrade fixture in the ordinary suite. Validate
healthy old IDs/maps through input-only update/switch/restart, positive root
backing and old valid dependent layouts, missing declared backing/wrong live
mount refusal, source metadata and fresh preparation. No new storage policy,
block devices, account repair, persisted format, host coordination or new runner.

Prior29e268350 image workflow38582595251 passed all six cases; that evidence
covers corrected images, not migration from an existing old guest. Revised
product tests still need final committed review and exact-head runtime. Policy
source edits do not authorize package activation, integration or KB publication.

The user explicitly requested GPT-6 Astra/xhigh assessment of the whole
persistence mechanism, including inherited mount promotion, host/image
responsibilities and upstream impermanence, rather than only the newest fix.
Fresh standalone reviewer `/root/astra_persistence_review` was launched with

and changed no files, refs or runtime state. The collaboration launch settings
are the model/effort evidence; the reviewer had no separate introspection API.

## Findings

1. **Important: selection omits valid persistence declarations.** Exact
   `/var/lib/nixos` and `/var/log` systemd binds enable the guard, while a sole
   `/var` or `/var/lib` bind or direct `fileSystems` declaration can leave users
   before specialfs. Pinned impermanence explicitly recognizes allocation-state
   ancestors (`nixos.nix:598`). This is source-established missing coverage,
   not a newly reproduced failure or a rejection of the supplied-layout passes.
2. **Advisory: bootstrap source metadata is permanent.** The adapter creates
   missing sources as root/0755. Pinned `create-directories.bash:46-53` applies
   configured metadata only when the source is absent. Actual fresh runtime
   `testct-a498` requested0710 but retained `0:0:755:384` in machine-shell.log
   near5283. Snapshot equality alone accepted the initial value. Documentation's
   later-metadata promise was misleading; custom owner and mode need an owner.
3. **Advisory: recursive directory preparation might use scoped mkdir-p.** This
   was conditional on equivalence. Architect0's follow-up found different
   missing-parent behavior under inherited default ACLs; the accepted refinement
   keeps the existing helper rather than changing that metadata contract.

## Architectural conclusion

Keep guest-owned persistence, host-provided storage and upstream global early
mount ordering. The absence of initrd, LXC's existing proc mount, impermanence's
after-users source creation and NixOS's continuing ERR trap explain why a bare
dependency edge is insufficient for both fresh sources and failed mounts.
The whole-value specialfs seam is awkward but proportionate at the supported
pins. Moving guest persistence policy into osctld, forcing another account
backend/fixed IDs, changing only the proc guard or adding another mount
framework would not provide a simpler compatible solution.

The minimum invariant is that the first legacy allocator invocation sees the
intended state, fresh sources can initialize, failed required mounts cannot
masquerade as fresh state, and repeated activation preserves existing state and
mount relationships. The scope gap, metadata ownership and missing tests should
be refined within that adapter. There are no migrations or coordinated host
updates. Rollback can restore the ordering defect; drifted identities need
separate recovery.

The user chose root/0755 defaults, custom owner AND mode pre-provisioning, then
approved the implementation plan. Architect0 recorded the accepted brief in
`design.md` (initial revision SHA256
`c80fea979d8fe48c48d98b78a81b21dd8ea596e31d0c45e8eda296abdb1382b9`).
It covers effective state-covering mounts and required predecessor membership
using existing `utils.fsBefore`, checked bind/nonbind handling, precise source

The user authorized implementation through the lead. This document records the
accepted decisions before application edits; verification below is planned
unless explicitly identified as completed evidence.

## Scope and ownership

Streamline the NixOS guest compatibility interface in `vpsadminos`, including
generated guest flakes and documentation. Stable guests should retain the same
import while changing their nixpkgs release. Explicit release imports must use
literal NixOS release strings without transforming dots into underscores.

The architect owns this brief and consequential design revisions. The
implementer owns application changes assigned by the lead. The lead owns
plan/state, the initial tracking commit, worktree and branch orchestration,
bilingual KB candidates, verification coordination, review and publication.
Refer material deviations to the lead before implementing them.

The original import design used canonical `origin/staging` commit
`1150e37b1cc997b1728f2fda806a3433ef55b798`. The current persistence revision uses
the exact reviewed source and evidence recorded below. No configuration-repository change
is expected. Final review expanded the scope to a narrow
`vpsfree-kb-contracts` companion change: bind both Impermanence pages to the

`implementer0` owns the contract bindings and minimal related metadata. This
revision does not change the guest-module architecture or technical APIs.

runtime CI and required establishing its root cause. The bounded correction
below supersedes the original prohibition on raw compatibility changes for
this defect only. It is a separate logical baseline-fix commit. It does not
change the import interface, guest pins, stateVersion or KB scope. The lead
accepted the compatibility-preserving callback revision below, superseding
mechanism B and its non-root backing requirement. The user authorized this
revision and normal test organization. After the independent whole-approach
review, the user authorized the effective-mount selection and verification
revision below. This is the current persistence design. The lead retains
implementation assignment and the separate instruction rollback/history work;
checks remain planned unless explicitly recorded as completed.

## Public interface

`containerStable` is the canonical spelling in generated stable templates and
KB examples. `container` remains an equivalent selector alias.

| Export | Accepted behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `nixosModules.containers."26.05"` | Exact versioned stable compatibility module |
| `nixosModules.containers.${nixpkgs.lib.trivial.release}` | Explicit lookup using the guest nixpkgs input |
| `nixosModules.containerStable` | Select a known stable module using the guest module-system `lib.trivial.release` |
| `nixosModules.container` | The same selector as `containerStable` |
| `nixosModules.container_26_05` and other existing underscore exports | Retained exact version aliases |
| `nixosModules.containerUnstable` | Existing explicit unstable module |
| `nixosConfigurations.container` and `containerStable` | Existing latest-stable module, independent of guest release |

Retained release exports do not imply current upstream security support for
those releases. Do not add `containerAuto`, flat release exports or an automatic
fallback to unstable.

## Release map and selection invariants

Maintain one explicit internal release map to the existing versioned files.
Expose that map as `nixosModules.containers` and derive every underscore version
alias from it. The error's supported-release list also comes from the map.
Do not independently maintain three lists of releases, aliases and error text.

Both modern generic aliases reference one module selector with this shape:

```nix
{ lib, ... }:
{
  imports = [
    (releaseModules.${lib.trivial.release} or (throw unsupportedReleaseMessage))
  ];
}
```

The error must identify the unsupported release, list the known stable releases,
and advise updating the vpsadminos input or explicitly selecting
`containerUnstable` when using unstable. Failure occurs during evaluation before
building or activation. Direct lookup of a missing grouped key may retain Nix's
ordinary missing-attribute error; the actionable error is the selector contract.

Use the `lib` supplied by the guest's module evaluator. Do not choose from
vpsadminos's captured nixpkgs library, `pkgs.lib`, `config.system.nixos.release`,
`config.system.stateVersion` or another `_module.args` value. Imports are
collected before configuration options can be evaluated. The built-in `lib`
argument is available at that stage; option-dependent imports can recurse.
`system.stateVersion` controls persisted-behavior compatibility and is not the
current guest software release. No new module option or special argument is
needed.

Do not infer unstable from `lib.trivial.version` containing `pre`. The inspected
stable flake input at `7993f34ee47e28a3d607a525aadc6c94b73be728` reports
`release = "26.05"` and `version = "26.05pre-git"`: nixpkgs uses `pre-git`
when the source lacks `.version-suffix`. Stable-only selection means that the
selector returns only a versioned stable module. It does not prove branch
provenance: an unstable snapshot reporting a known release number will also
select that stable module. Unstable users must explicitly import
`containerUnstable`.

Preserve the original latest-stable binding for the two legacy
`nixosConfigurations` aliases: it imports `stable/vpsadminos.nix`. This is an
intentional distinction from the release map, not a second version table. Do not
derive legacy latest stable from a caller's release or an overrideable flake
input. The unstable binding remains independent as well.

## Grouped-map convention and validation

The grouped map is a documented extension to the usual convention that each
`nixosModules.<name>` is one importable module. Each release leaf is a module;
`nixosModules.containers` itself is a lookup map and must not be imported.
Generic consumers that import every value of `nixosModules` cannot assume this
new member is a module. Do not introduce `__functor` or another callable wrapper
to disguise the map.

In [Nix 2.34.8's checker](https://github.com/NixOS/nix/blob/2.34.8/src/nix/flake.cc#L449),
the module check only forces each top-level value; its
[output traversal](https://github.com/NixOS/nix/blob/2.34.8/src/nix/flake.cc#L661)
does not validate nested release leaves. A successful flake check therefore
cannot replace focused leaf/module evaluations. The pre-existing
`nixosConfigurations` exports are module functions rather than evaluated system
configurations; a full flake check can fail on that independent convention
mismatch. Record the baseline instead of changing legacy exports to make the
whole check pass.

## Grouped-map convention and validation

The grouped map is a documented extension to the usual convention that each
`nixosModules.<name>` is one importable module. Each release leaf is a module;
`nixosModules.containers` itself is a lookup map and must not be imported.
Generic consumers that import every value of `nixosModules` cannot assume this
new member is a module. Do not introduce `__functor` or another callable wrapper
to disguise the map.

In [Nix 2.34.8's checker](https://github.com/NixOS/nix/blob/2.34.8/src/nix/flake.cc#L449),
the module check only forces each top-level value; its
[output traversal](https://github.com/NixOS/nix/blob/2.34.8/src/nix/flake.cc#L661)
does not validate nested release leaves. A successful flake check therefore
cannot replace focused leaf/module evaluations. The pre-existing
`nixosConfigurations` exports are module functions rather than evaluated system
configurations; a full flake check can fail on that independent convention
mismatch. Record the baseline instead of changing legacy exports to make the
whole check pass.

### Required predecessor membership and checked dispatch

A dependency edge orders snippets but does not make a failed prerequisite stop
allocation: NixOS's ERR trap records failure and continues. Presence also cannot
prove that an earlier failed remount succeeded. Derive a finite required set
from the selected state mounts and their transitive predecessors under the
existing `utils.fsBefore` relation over the effective early entries.

Use a standard finite closure keyed by effective `mountPoint` (for example
`lib.genericClosure`), starting with selected mounts and adding each existing
entry `a` for which `utils.fsBefore a b` holds for a visited entry `b`. Deduplicate
by that key; cycles must terminate this membership calculation and remain an
upstream mount-order error. This set answers only which existing callbacks must
fail closed. It must not order, schedule, replay or introduce any mount. It
covers source and destination ancestry and explicit `depends`, including a
backing bind whose own source resides on another early mount.

Dispatch from the effective entry and its configured tuple, not original
`what`/`where` plus `fsType == "none"`. Identify directory binds from `bind` or
`rbind` option tokens, retaining the configured tokens and all other options.
Handle callbacks as follows:

| Entry | Required behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Selected directory bind | Validate required backing availability; prepare only missing source/target directories; validate live directory identity; check configured bind/remount and final mountpoint/identity |
| Selected non-bind filesystem | Never create or compare the device/UUID/network source as a directory; prepare only an absent target, preserve existing metadata, check configured mount/remount and final exact mountpoint |
| Required predecessor | Preserve its existing mount/remount type/options and position, but explicitly propagate failed preparation/mount/remount; do not create missing source directories; verify exact mountpoint and directory-bind identity where applicable |
| Unrelated early mount | Retain the ordinary upstream callback behavior |

Root and pseudo-filesystem entries may be required predecessors without becoming
selection seeds. Keep their native mount handling; do not add non-root or
durability checks. Checked directory targets retain existing owner/mode/content;
only missing targets receive normal defaults. No unrelated callback gains a
blanket failure policy. Document the small upstream callback's maintenance
responsibility near its copied shell body.

Every failed required callback or state prerequisite explicitly exits the parent

not rely on `set -e` inside conditionally called functions. Dry activation does
no preparation or mount work. This guarantees no legacy allocation in the failed
activation, not that every stage-2 path or later service universally stops on a
nonzero activation status.

### Directory identity and storage limits

Before selected source creation, effective early mountpoints covering that
source must already be present as exact mountpoints. Use path components,
including `/`, rather than guessed first components. A declared covering
`bind`/`rbind` requires both source and target to resolve to directories and
`[ "$backingSource" -ef "$backingMountPoint" ]`. Do not create an absent
backing source. The same identity rule applies to checked directory-bind
prerequisites; it catches a different live bind surviving an ordinary remount.
A directory alias resolving to the same object is valid. Failure must precede
selected-source creation and allocation, even when a mountpoint already exists.

For a selected bind with an already-mounted destination, require source/target
identity before remounting. A mismatch is refused without stacking, replacing
or unmounting the live bind. For an unmounted target, create only missing
directories and perform the configured bind. Check the mount command, exact
mountpoint and directory identity afterward. Preserve quoted arguments and
configured source, destination, type and options. An ancestor bind needs only
its own source prepared; the real legacy allocator creates `/var/lib/nixos`
inside the mounted ancestor. Do not add a separate map-directory initializer.

For non-bind filesystems, check the actual mount/remount result and exact
mountpoint; do not apply directory `-ef` to a block device, UUID or network
source. This retains the upstream source-mount contract without promising
universal device identity validation. Directory identity likewise does not
prove recursive mount-tree equivalence or future durability.

The supplied `/persistent` is an osctld host dataset bind, not a guest block
device. Sources on persistent `/` or custom binds remain supported. Undeclared
host storage retains its prior availability contract: stale directories exposed
by an absent undeclared host bind can look identical to a valid root-backed
layout. Mount IDs, device IDs, directory existence and map presence cannot prove
intended durability. Do not add a storage policy, impermanence-schema probing or
heuristic to conceal that limit. Earlier unrelated callbacks may already have
run before a failure; no claim of an entirely inert failed activation is made.

# NixOS guests

NixOS guests need a compatibility module to boot and use networking supplied by
the vpsAdminOS host. Import it from the vpsAdminOS flake, or download the
self-contained module for your guest's release.

## Stable flake imports

Use `vpsadminos.nixosModules.containerStable` in the guest's module list:

```nix
{
  inputs = {
    nixpkgs.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-26.05";
    vpsadminos.url = "github:vpsfreecz/vpsadminos";
  };

  outputs = { nixpkgs, vpsadminos, ... }: {
    nixosConfigurations.vps = nixpkgs.lib.nixosSystem {
      system = "x86_64-linux";
      modules = [
        vpsadminos.nixosModules.containerStable
        ./configuration.nix
      ];
    };
  };
}
```

The selector uses the guest's nixpkgs release. The import can stay unchanged
when you upgrade the guest to another known stable release. `nixosModules.container` is an equivalent alias.

Selection is independent of `system.stateVersion`. Keep that setting at the
value appropriate for your installation; changing the guest's nixpkgs release
does not require changing stateVersion. The vpsAdminOS flake's own nixpkgs input
also does not determine which guest module is selected.

The release map contains `22.11`, `23.05`, `23.11`, `24.05`,
`24.11`, `25.05`, `25.11` and `26.05`. These modules remain available for
compatibility; their availability does not imply upstream security support.
You can select a release explicitly with a literal key:

```nix
vpsadminos.nixosModules.containers."26.05"
```

Or use the guest nixpkgs input's release without converting dots to underscores:

```nix
vpsadminos.nixosModules.containers.${nixpkgs.lib.trivial.release}
```

Each leaf is an importable module. `nixosModules.containers` is a lookup map and
must not itself be imported. Consumers that enumerate `nixosModules` must handle
this map separately.

An unknown release fails during evaluation. The selector's error names the
release, lists known releases and advises updating the vpsAdminOS input or
selecting the explicit unstable module. There is no fallback to unstable.
Direct lookup of a missing grouped key produces Nix's missing-attribute error.

## Unstable guests

Use `vpsadminos.nixosModules.containerUnstable` with nixpkgs unstable. The stable
selector uses the release number and cannot identify the source branch. If an
unstable snapshot reports a known stable release number, the stable selector
chooses that release's module. A version suffix such as `pre-git` also does not
reliably identify unstable.

## Existing imports and generated configurations

Existing underscore exports such as `nixosModules.container_24_11` continue to
import the named release module. The legacy exports
`nixosConfigurations.container` and `nixosConfigurations.containerStable` keep
using the raw latest-stable module, independently of the guest release.
`nixosConfigurations.containerUnstable` remains the explicit unstable module.
These legacy values are modules, rather than evaluated NixOS systems.

Stable image templates generate `nixosModules.containerStable`; unstable
templates generate `nixosModules.containerUnstable`. The ordinary and
impermanence variants use the same choice. First boot copies configuration files
only when they are absent, so an image update does not rewrite an existing
guest configuration.

The grouped exports and release-aware selectors require a vpsAdminOS revision
that provides this interface. Earlier revisions accept `containerStable` but
use their latest-stable module. Keep the generated lockfile, or lock an
appropriate published revision before relying on the selector.

## Standalone module

For a configuration without the flake import, download the versioned stable file
matching the guest's release, for example:

```sh
curl -o /etc/nixos/vpsadminos.nix \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vpsfreecz/vpsadminos/staging/os/lib/nixos-container/stable/vpsadminos-26.05.nix
```

Import `./vpsadminos.nix` from the guest configuration. The raw versioned files,
`stable/vpsadminos.nix` (latest stable), and `unstable/vpsadminos.nix` are each
self-contained; no companion files are required. A downloaded file cannot
automatically select another release. The root
`os/lib/nixos-container/vpsadminos.nix` is a guard and is not the download target.

## Changing an existing guest import

Update the vpsAdminOS input to a revision with this interface, change the import,
and evaluate the configuration with the existing guest nixpkgs pin and
stateVersion before activation. Compare the result with the matching explicit
release module. Guests adopt independently when rebuilt; no coordinated update
of hosts or running nodes is required.

Keep the prior lockfile and NixOS generations for recovery. Reverting to a
vpsAdminOS revision without grouped exports also requires reverting grouped
imports. To restore former latest-stable behavior for a modern generic import,
restore the prior vpsAdminOS pin or choose an appropriate explicit module.
The import change introduces no persisted state or data conversion. A separate
NixOS release upgrade retains that release's normal rollback constraints.

## Persistent allocation state

The 25.11, 26.05, latest stable and unstable compatibility modules establish
early mounts covering `/var/lib/nixos` or `/var/log` before legacy user
allocation. This includes persistence of `/var` or `/var/lib` and mounts
declared through `fileSystems`, as well as impermanence directory binds. The
effective `boot.specialFileSystems` declarations determine which mounts run.
Root `/` is already available when activation starts and does not by itself
enable this adapter.

LXC mounts `/proc` before starting init, which causes NixOS to skip its early
mount path. User allocation must see the saved maps before it runs; mounting
them later leaves newly allocated IDs in `/etc/passwd` and `/etc/group` while
exposing the original maps and file ownership on persistent storage.

The compatibility module uses NixOS's global early-mount order. For selected
directory binds, it creates only absent source directories and parents, with
root ownership and mode 0755. Existing content, ownership and modes remain
untouched. Pre-provision sources that need another owner or mode. Impermanence
uses existing source metadata; it does not later apply the configured owner or
mode to a source that this adapter has already created.

Sources can reside on persistent `/` or on a separate backing mount. The supplied
images use the host-mounted `/persistent` dataset; guests need no block device
or storage-layout change. For backing mounts declared in NixOS's early mount
set, activation checks that the covering mountpoints are present before
creating source directories. Declared directory binds must also match their
configured source directory. A failed selected mount, or a mount it depends
on, stops activation before legacy allocation, including a failed remount whose
target remains mounted. A directory bind destination mounted from a different
source also stops activation. Matching live binds retain their source and
configured remount options.

Selected filesystems of other types and their prerequisites retain their
configured mount/remount operations and require a successful operation and a
mounted destination. Their device, UUID or
network source is not treated as a directory. These checks do not establish
arbitrary device identity or durability; for example, an explicitly configured
tmpfs at `/var` still provides temporary storage.

Host-supplied storage that has no guest early-mount declaration must already be
available. The guest cannot distinguish an intentionally root-backed directory
from stale directories exposed when an undeclared host mount is missing. Mount
presence and directory identity do not prove that storage will survive a host
failure.

A healthy guest can adopt by updating its vpsAdminOS input or downloaded module
and rebuilding with its existing nixpkgs pin, stateVersion and storage layout.
Guests adopt independently without host coordination. Sysusers and userborn
keep their existing activation paths. An explicit guest replacement of the
specialfs activation script remains responsible for its own mount behavior.

This preserves identities in healthy guests. It does not recover a guest whose
UIDs or GIDs have already changed.
Before rebuilding such a guest, compare and save its account IDs, allocation
maps and persistent dataset. A rebuild can replace the saved maps with the
current drifted IDs. Account or file ownership repair requires a separate
recovery decision. Earlier generations still read the same map format, but a
rollback restart can reintroduce the ordering defect.

16531-27.5 Directories and the Set-User-ID and Set-Group-ID Bits
16532-==========================================================
16533-
16534-On most systems, if a directory's set-group-ID bit is set, newly created
16535-subfiles inherit the same group as the directory, and newly created
16536-subdirectories inherit the set-group-ID bit of the parent directory.  On
16537-a few systems, a directory's set-user-ID bit has a similar effect on the
16538-ownership of new subfiles and the set-user-ID bits of new
16539-subdirectories.  These mechanisms let users share files more easily, by
16540-lessening the need to use ‘chmod’ or ‘chown’ to share new files.
16541-
16542-   These convenience mechanisms rely on the set-user-ID and set-group-ID
16543-bits of directories.  If commands like ‘chmod’ and ‘mkdir’ routinely
16544-cleared these bits on directories, the mechanisms would be less
16545-convenient and it would be harder to share files.  Therefore, a command
16546-like ‘chmod’ does not affect the set-user-ID or set-group-ID bits of a
16547-directory unless the user specifically mentions them in a symbolic mode,
16548-or uses an operator numeric mode such as ‘=755’, or sets them in a
16549-numeric mode, or clears them in a numeric mode that has five or more
16550-octal digits.  For example, on systems that support set-group-ID
16551-inheritance:
16552-
16553-     # These commands leave the set-user-ID and
16554-     # set-group-ID bits of the subdirectories alone,
16555-     # so that they retain their default values.
16556-     mkdir A B C
16557-     chmod 755 A
16558-     chmod 0755 B
16559-     chmod u=rwx,go=rx C
16560-     mkdir -m 755 D
16561-     mkdir -m 0755 E
16562-     mkdir -m u=rwx,go=rx F
16563-
16564-   If you want to try to set these bits, you must mention them
16565-explicitly in the symbolic or numeric modes, e.g.:
16566-
16567-     # These commands try to set the set-user-ID
16568-     # and set-group-ID bits of the subdirectories.
16569-     mkdir G
16570-     chmod 6755 G
16571-     chmod +6000 G
16572-     chmod u=rwx,go=rx,a+s G
16573-     mkdir -m 6755 H
16574-     mkdir -m +6000 I
16575-     mkdir -m u=rwx,go=rx,a+s J
16576-
16577-   If you want to try to clear these bits, you must mention them
16578-explicitly in a symbolic mode, or use an operator numeric mode, or
16579-specify a numeric mode with five or more octal digits, e.g.:
16580-
16581-     # These commands try to clear the set-user-ID
16582-     # and set-group-ID bits of the directory D.
16583-     chmod a-s D
16584-     chmod -6000 D
16585-     chmod =755 D
16586-     chmod 00755 D
16587-
16588-   This behavior is a GNU extension.  Portable scripts should not rely
16589-on requests to set or clear these bits on directories, as POSIX allows
